'''Carlos José Bustamante''' (born 1951 in [[Lima]], [[Peru]]) is a Peruvian-American [[scientist]]. He is a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos J. Bustamante |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/carlos-j-bustamante-hbhzhe/ |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlos Bustamante {{!}} Physics |url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/carlos-bustamante |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=physics.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==
Carlos Bustamante is a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] (HHMI) investigator,<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos J. Bustamante, PhD |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/carlos-j-bustamante |website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute|accessdate=28 July 2020}}</ref> [[professor]] of [[Molecular biology|molecular]] and cell biology, [[physics]], and [[chemistry]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos J. Bustamante |url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/bustamante |website=University of California Berkeley}}</ref> and Biophysicist Faculty Scientist at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos Bustamante |url=https://biosciences.lbl.gov/profiles/carlos-bustamante/ |website=Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory}}</ref>

Bustamante studied medicine in Peru at [[National University of San Marcos]] before discovering his true interest in biochemistry. He received his BSc from [[Cayetano Heredia University]] in Lima, his MSc in [[biochemistry]] from [[National University of San Marcos]] in Lima, and his PhD in [[biophysics]] from [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]], where he studied with [[Ignacio Tinoco, Jr.]] As a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], Bustamante studied with Marcos Maestre. Before moving to Berkeley, he was an [[HHMI]] investigator at the [[University of Oregon]] after serving as an assistant and associate professor in the University of New Mexico Department of Chemistry from 1982 to 1986.

==Research focus==
Carlos Bustamante develops and uses novel methods of [[single-molecule]] [[Chemical imaging|visualization]], such as scanning force microscopy, to study the structure and function of [[nucleoprotein]] assemblies. His laboratory is developing methods of [[single-molecule experiment|single-molecule manipulation]], such as [[optical tweezers]], to characterize the elasticity of [[DNA]], to induce the mechanical unfolding of individual [[protein]] [[molecules]], and to investigate the machine-like behavior of molecular motors. Currently at UC Berkeley they are using the single-molecule manipulation method to study how protein-DNA and the process of gene expression are related.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlos Bustamante {{!}} Physics |url=https://physics.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/carlos-bustamante |access-date=2026-01-18 |website=physics.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

Bustamante’s laboratory was the first to mechanically manipulate and stretch a single molecule of DNA using optical tweezers to measure its elastic properties, it was essential to his studies of molecular machines such as RNA polymerase and ribosomes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Carlos Bustamante, PhD |url=https://thevalleefoundation.org/programs/vvp/carlos-bustamante-phd |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=Vallee Foundation}}</ref>

A 2005 publication <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bustamante |first=Carlos |last2=Liphardt |first2=Jan |last3=Ritort |first3=Felix |date=2005-07-01 |title=The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Small Systems |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2012462 |journal=Physics Today |volume=58 |issue=7 |pages=43–48 |doi=10.1063/1.2012462 |issn=0031-9228|arxiv=cond-mat/0511629 }}</ref> demonstrates RNA polymerase activity in using thermodynamic energy fluctuations to accomplish RNA transcription.

==Positions==
* Assistant professor, department of chemistry, [[University of New Mexico]] (1982–1986)
* Associate professor, department of chemistry, [[University of New Mexico]] (1986–1989)
* Professor of chemistry, department of chemistry, [[University of New Mexico]] (1989–1990)
* Professor of chemistry and member of the Institute of Molecular Biology, [[University of Oregon]] (1991–1998)
* Professor in molecular and cell biology, chemistry, and physics, [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] (1998–present)
* Honorary professor, [[National University of San Marcos]], Lima, Peru

==Fellowships and awards==
* [[Searle Scholar]] (1984)
* [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Fellow (1985)
* Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1995), Citation: ''For pioneering the application of optical methods and scanning probes in measurements of the properties of single DNA molecules.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2022-04-29 |website=aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Elected member, National Academy of Sciences, [[List of members of the National Academy of Sciences (Biophysics and computational biology)|Biophysics]] 2002
* [[Max Delbrück]] Prize in Biological Physics (2002)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honors and Award Winners |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Hans Neurath Award of the Protein Society (2004) 
* In 2005 he received the [[Richtmyer Memorial Award]] given annually by the [[American Association of Physics Teachers]].
* [[Alexander Hollaender Award in Biophysics]] (2004)<ref name=NAS>{{cite web|title=Alexander Hollaender Award in Biophysics|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_hollaender|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|accessdate=13 February 2011|url-status = dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101229194636/http://www.nasonline.org/site/PageServer?pagename=AWARDS_hollaender|archivedate=29 December 2010}}</ref>

* [[The Vilcek Foundation|Vilcek Prize in Biomedical Science]] (2012)<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Gems from Distant Shores: The 2012 Vilcek Foundation Prizes|journal = The FASEB Journal|date = 2012-04-01|issn = 0892-6638|pmid = 22467904|pages = 1361–1366|volume = 26|issue = 4|doi = 10.1096/fj.12-0402ufm|language = en|first1 = Prashant|last1 = Nair|first2 = Jan|last2 = Vilcek| doi-access=free |s2cid = 42079568}}</ref>
